items.description: La victoria del Barcelona ante el Alavés, después de dos derrotas contra PSG y Real Madrid, en Champions y LaLiga respectivamente, devolvió al conjunto azulgrana a la senda del triunfo y estuvo marcada sobre todo por la eficacia en ataque. La delantera barcelonista fue fulminante y destacaron sobre todo sendos dobletes de Raphinha y Lamine Yamal, que ampliaron unos registros goleadores que ya eran buenos antes del partido y ahora son de escándalo en lo que va de temporada. Entre los dos, veinticinco tantos en LaLiga y cuatro en Champions. Veintinueve goles en catorce partidos entre los dos. Cuando tienen el punto de mira afinado, la eficiencia del equipo de Flick está a buen recaudo.

items.title: El árbitro del derbi se defiende: "Veo penalti claro de cerca y el VAR confirma mi decisión"
items.description: Como novedad de esta jornada, al árbitro del derbi vasco, Alejandro Hernández Hernández, le tocó dar explicaciones al término del derbi vasco en DAZN y se defendió de la principal decisión del encuentro, que fue el penalti de Aramburu sobre Nico Williams que dio el derbi al Athletic y condenó a la Real Sociedad. "Es una acción de pase entre líneas, en profundidad, llego bien, me pilla la jugada a 4 metros, es una acción que se puede analizar como dentro o fuera. Me pilla justo a la altura de la línea lateral del área de penalti para peritar si la acción es dentro o fuera. Veo que el delantero, Nico Williams, hace el dribbling, el regate, y el jugador de la Real Sociedad, Jon, impacta con él de una forma que yo considero punible. Y por esa razón, de forma inmediata pito penalti, porque para mí en el campo en ese momento fue penalti claro", comentó en primera instancia, explicando su visión.

items.title: Disparate en Bilbao
items.description: El partido de la Real en San Mamés no fue brillante, no está claro que fuera suficiente para merecer algo más. Los txuri urdin venían en una racha increíble, estaban bien posicionados y con confianza pero podían perder en Bilbao. Entraba dentro de lo factible ante un buen equipo en su casa. Pero lo que es más que evidente es que, una vez más, el derbi vasco en San Mamés estuvo marcado por el equipo arbitral. No solo por la acción decisiva en sí, sino porque fue cuando la Real mejor estaba, habiéndose rehecho de un mal inicio. No es cuestión de señalar a un Alejandro Hernández Hernández que estuvo fatal pero que podía ver en directo infracción, sino a todos sus compañeros, tanto los que le acompañaron en Bilbao como los que estaban en una sala en Madrid, incluso a los que gestionan, dirigen y detallan normativas, protocolos y todo lo demás. La Real tuvo la ‘fortuna’, además, de que este derbi fuera el que estrenara, en DAZN, las explicaciones pospartido del árbitro. Peor todavía, al tener que ver y escuchar justificaciones que se alejan de la realidad y que contrastan, además, con la opinión hasta del entrenador rival, que fue un señor reconociendo sentirse beneficiado. La cara de incredulidad de Aramburu al ver cómo pitaban penalti y lo confirmaban desde el VAR solo puede ser superada por la que no se vio, del propio venezolano, viendo la repetición al acabar el encuentro. Sensación de injusticia, impotencia e incomprensión. Se acaba la racha de derbis de la manera más incendiaria pero la Real tiene que seguir, porque tiene un partido muy importante el jueves.

items.title: Rajada descomunal de Aramburu por el penalti del derbi: "Es una injusticia, el VAR le dice que no toco balón"
items.description: Jon Mikel Aramburu, lateral de la Real Sociedad, alucinó en directo con la pena máxima señalada por Alejandro Hernández Hernández en San Mamés, que no corrigió el VAR, y que sentenció el derbi a favor del Athletic. Pero se mantuvo terriblemente enfadado tras el término del encuentro, manifestando su descontento claro y explicando además los detalles de la acción y la situación. La rajada es clara e ilustrativa. "Todos los derbis son disputados. Sabíamos que iba a ser así, un partido que se iba a definir por detalles. Creemos que el penalti es una acción que no es penalti. Me acaban de enseñar con el chip que toco el balón, el árbitro afirma que yo no toco el balón, pero tiene toda la tecnología. Me parece increíble que pite un penalti así cuando claramente la toco yo. Hasta Nico lo decía, que para él no era penalti, pero bueno, es una pena que se haya tenido que decidir por una situación polémica. Nico decía que el toque era mínimo y que yo había tocado el balón. Yo le decía a Nico que he tocado el balón y el árbitro lo único que dice es que 'es penalti confirmado porque en el VAR me han dicho que no tocas el balón'. Me acaban de enseñar una jugada con el chip en la televisión, donde claramente toco el balón. Entonces hay que aclararse un poco porque para mí es una injusticia", contó el lateral realista.

items.title: Iribar y Kortabarria reviven en San Mamés el acto más icónico del fútbol vasco
items.description: San Mamés ha revivido un imagen icónica en los prolegómenos del derbi. José Ángel Iribar e Inaxio Kortabarria han salido al césped con una Ikurriña mientras la que sacaron aquel 5 de diciembre de 1976 en Atotxa, el entonces el campo de la Real, estaba en un atril. Han pasado 50 años desde entonces, pero hay imágenes que quedan grababas para siempre en la memoria colectiva de los dos clubs y del fútbol vasco. Esta es una de ellas. Un símbolo que mantiene intacto su valor histórico y social y un tributo a la iniciativa de 1976, recién salidos de una dictadura de 40 años.

items.title: Real Madrid
items.description: Le Real Madrid est un club de football espagnol fondé en 1902. Le Real est le club le plus titré de l'histoire en Ligue des champions avec 14 sacres. A son palmarès également, 35 titres de champion d'Espagne, 19 Coupes du roi notamment. items.title: El Racing de Santander será multado por el lanzamiento del mechero
items.description: La derrota en casa del Racing de Santander ante el Real Madrid por 3-0 traerá además una multa para el equipo cántabro. Sanción como consecuencia del lanzamiento de un mechero desde la grada. Incidente que se produjo tras la revisión en el VAR de José Luis Munuera Montero de una posible mano de Tchouameni dentro del área y que finalmente determinó que no era motivo de ser sancionada con pena máxima. Lanzamiento del objeto que el colegiado recogió así en el acta arbitral: "En el minuto 78, se activó la fase 1 del protocolo de lanzamiento de objetos, debido al lanzamiento de un mechero procedente de la grada, cayendo cerca del asistente número dos, sin llegar a impactarle". Protocolo consistente en avisarlo por megafonía.

"Cuando el árbitro ha pitado el penalti a Mbappé estaba muy tranquilo porque a sesenta metros no podía verlo. Pero después cuando lo he visto repetido en el ipad he dicho: "si el VAR no está dormido, no es penalti", reconoció Mourinho. items.title: Liverpool vs Arsenal: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Premier League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Liverpool vs Arsenal in the 2026-27 Premier League. Liverpool and Arsenal meet with both sides carrying long injury lists into a fixture that still carries heavy weight in the title picture.
Liverpool head into this one off a 2-0 win over Albion on October 25, following a 2-1 victory against Brentford on October 17. Before that run started, they were beaten 0-3 by Man City on October 11, a reminder of how costly a bad day against a top side can be. Three points here would settle any lingering nerves from that City defeat and keep Iraola’s side firmly in the mix.
Arsenal arrive on the back of three straight wins, beating Everton 2-0 on October 24 after a 1-0 result against Nottingham on October 18. They also won 2-1 at Leeds on October 10, so Arteta’s team have not dropped points in any of their last three outings. A result at Anfield would extend that run against the toughest opponent they have faced in it.
Liverpool confirmed lineup
Iraola sets Liverpool up in a 4-2-3-1 but is without a long list of regulars, including Dominik Szoboszlai, Conor Bradley and Jeremie Frimpong, which pushes Ronald Araujo into the back four alongside Virgil Van Dijk and Jérémy Jacquet. Gravenberch and Mac Allister anchor midfield behind a front line of Wirtz, Barcola and Gakpo supporting Isak, with the absence of Hugo Ekitiké making Isak the clear focal point up top. The depth missing at full-back and in attack means Liverpool have less rotation to call on if the game state changes.
Liverpool confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Alisson, Ronald Araujo, Jérémy Jacquet, Virgil Van Dijk, Miloš Kerkez, Alexis Mac Allister, Florian Wirtz, Treymaurice Nyoni, Bradley Barcola, Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo. Coach: Andoni Iraola.
Arsenal confirmed lineup
Arteta also lines Arsenal up in a 4-2-3-1, missing Bukayo Saka and William Saliba, two significant absences that reshape both ends of the pitch. Gabriel Magalhães and Ben White take on extra responsibility in defense without Saliba, while Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke flank Havertz in a front three built to compensate for Saka’s absence. Rice and Guimarães sit in front of the back four to shield that reshuffled defense, with Odegaard tasked with linking play between midfield and attack.
Arsenal confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): David Raya, Jurriën Timber, Ezri Konsa, Gabriel Magalhães, Riccardo Calafiori, Declan Rice, Martín Odegaard, Bruno Guimarães, Noni Madueke, Kai Havertz, Christos Tzolis. Coach: Mikel Arteta.

items.title: Santander vs Real Madrid: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 LaLiga match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Santander vs Real Madrid in the 2026-27 LaLiga. Santander host a Real Madrid side that has not lost since early October, and the gap in form between these two clubs is hard to ignore heading into this one.
Santander come into this match off a 2-1 win over Espanyol on October 24, but that followed a 0-2 loss to Osasuna on October 18 and a 2-2 draw with Valencia on October 11. The mixed run leaves them with just one win in three outings. A positive result here would give José Alberto López’s side real momentum before the next round of fixtures.
Real Madrid, on the other hand, have won three straight, including a 2-1 victory over Barcelona on October 25 that followed a 4-1 win against Sevilla on October 18 and a 1-0 result over Villarreal on October 10. That stretch has Real Madrid rolling into Santander full of confidence. A win here would make it four in a row and keep them firmly in the title picture.
Santander confirmed lineup
José Alberto López sets Santander up in a 4-2-3-1, with Iván Martín and Pablo García screening the back line and Sergio Canales given license to link play behind Yassir Zabiri. Iñigo Vicente and Matteo Prati provide width and movement off the flanks, while Jeanuël Belocian and Pablo Ramón Parra anchor the central defense in front of goalkeeper Julen Agirrezabala. Jorge Salinas is out, which removes an option from the squad, but the rest of the projected XI is at full strength.
Santander confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Julen Agirrezabala, Álvaro Mantilla, Pablo Ramón Parra, Jeanuël Belocian, Aarón Martín, Iván Martín, Sergio Canales, Matteo Prati, Iker Luque Sierra, Yassir Zabiri, Iñigo Vicente. Coach: José Alberto López.
Real Madrid confirmed lineup
José Mourinho lines Real Madrid up in a mirroring 4-2-3-1, with Aurélien Tchouaméni and Jude Bellingham holding the midfield while Arda Güler operates in the number 10 role behind Kylian Mbappé. Bernardo Silva and Yan Diomande offer width and pace in the final third, and the back four of Denzel Dumfries, Ibrahima Konaté, Dean Huijsen and Marc Cucurella protects Thibaut Courtois. Real Madrid are without Ferland Mendy, Raúl Asencio, Rodrygo and Vinícius Júnior, a notable list of absences that forces some reshuffling in defense and attack, though the depth of the starting group remains considerable.
Real Madrid confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Thibaut Courtois, Trent Alexander-Arnold, Dean Huijsen, Ibrahima Konaté, Marc Cucurella, Aurélien Tchouaméni, Jude Bellingham, Bernardo Silva, Arda Güler, Kylian Mbappé, Yan Diomande. Coach: José Mourinho.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo could claim unique place in soccer history with next two headed strikes on road to 1,000-goal milestone
items.description:
The Portuguese forward has also moved closer to a historic scoring achievement that could further distinguish him from some of soccer's greatest goalscorers. 
Cristiano Ronaldo is approaching two remarkable milestones as he continues his career with Al-Nassr, with his pursuit of 1,000 official goals attracting plenty of attention. The Portuguese forward has also moved closer to a historic scoring achievement that could further distinguish him from some of soccer’s greatest goalscorers.



At 41, Ronaldo remains a major attacking threat in the Saudi Pro League, and his latest performances have added another dimension to his remarkable career statistics. Just a handful of headed goals could be enough to put him at the top of another all-time list.



Ronaldo’s aerial ability has been one of the defining features of his career, helping him score consistently for Manchester United, Real Madrid, Juventus, Al-Nassr, and Portugal. He has now scored 160 headed goals across his senior club and international career.



The milestone follows a productive spell in October, including his performances against Al-Faisaly and Al-Kholood. His header against Al-Kholood came during Al-Nassr‘s 5-3 Saudi Pro League victory on October 29, when he completed a second-half hat-trick and took his overall career tally to a reported 985 official goals.



This Cristiano Ronaldo header goal is one of the easiest and almost looks like a tap in, but believe me Messi could have let that ball go out of play😭 pic.twitter.com/aQVoyTO60T— TheFV (@futbolverdict) October 30, 2026 



Headers account for approximately 16% of Ronaldo’s career goals, underlining how important his aerial presence has been throughout his time at the highest level. His ability to time his jumps, generate power, and find space inside the penalty area has remained a significant weapon even into his 40s.



The historic record Ronaldo is chasing



The latest figures place Ronaldo within touching distance of a long-standing historical benchmark. Scottish soccer legend Jimmy McGrory is widely credited with 162 headed goals, according to IFAB’s historical list, leaving Ronaldo two behind the former Celtic striker.



McGrory built his reputation during the 1920s and 1930s, playing for Celtic between 1921 and 1937. His place at the top of the list has stood for generations, but Ronaldo now has a realistic opportunity to match and potentially surpass that total. Historical statistics from that period can be difficult to verify consistently, but his total of 162 remains a widely cited benchmark.



RankPlayerCountryYears ActiveHeader Goals1.Jimmy McGroryScotland1921–19371622.Cristiano RonaldoPortugal2002–present160



Ronaldo had reportedly reached 159 headed goals after scoring against Al-Faisaly on October 24, before adding another against Al-Kholood five days later. Two more headed goals would see him equal McGrory’s total, while a third would put him outright at the top of the list.



Ronaldo’s aerial ability has defied his age



Ronaldo’s position near the top of the list is particularly impressive given the length of his career. He has maintained his aerial threat across several leagues and different tactical systems, adapting his game while continuing to punish defenders inside the box.



Cristiano Ronaldo of team Al Nassr jumps for a header whilst under pressure



His physical attributes have always played an important role, but his success in the air also reflects anticipation, positioning, and timing. Those qualities have allowed him to remain dangerous from crosses and set pieces long after many forwards would have lost their place among the elite.



The Portuguese’s immediate challenge is to keep producing goals for Al-Nassr, with every appearance offering another opportunity to move closer to McGrory’s record. A short run of successful aerial finishes could see him make history before reaching the 1,000-goal milestone.

items.title: Is Raphinha playing today? Confirmed lineups for Barcelona vs Alaves in 2026-27 LaLiga season Matchday 11
items.description:
Barcelona face Alaves in Matchday 11 of the 2026-27 LaLiga season, where Raphinha is expected to start in attack for the home side. Barcelona host Alaves at a moment when both sides need to settle themselves after uneven weeks, and this one looks lopsided on paper before a ball is kicked. For this game, Hansi Flick is expected to field Raphinha to lead the home side’s attack

Barcelona lost 1-2 to Real Madrid on October 25, but that followed wins of 5-2 over Betis on October 17 and 3-0 over Getafe on October 10. The Clasico defeat snapped a run of attacking form that had produced eight goals in two matches. A win here would put that setback behind them and keep the pressure on at the top of the table.
Alaves have not won in their last three outings, drawing 1-1 with Malaga on October 23 after back-to-back losses, 1-2 to Celta Vigo on October 18 and 1-2 to Atlético on October 10. The draw at least stopped the bleeding after consecutive defeats. Quique Flores will want his side to show the same resilience against a Barcelona team desperate to bounce back.
Barcelona confirmed lineup
Hansi Flick sets Barcelona up in a 4-3-3 with Joan García in goal behind a back line of Brian Fariñas Pérez, Pau Cubarsí, Frenkie De Jong and João Cancelo. Pedri, Fermín López and Rodri make up the midfield three, giving the team control in possession, while Lamine Yamal and Raphinha provide width either side of Karim Adeyemi through the middle. The absences of Andreas Christensen, Eric García, Xavi Espart, Dani Olmo, Roony Bardghji and Juan Hernández leave Flick short of options in defense and in reserve attacking depth, but the projected XI still carries plenty of quality going forward.
Barcelona confirmed starting XI (4-3-3): Joan García, Brian Fariñas Pérez, Pau Cubarsí, Frenkie De Jong, João Cancelo, Pedri, Fermín López, Rodri, Lamine Yamal, Raphinha, Karim Adeyemi. Coach: Hansi Flick.
Alaves confirmed lineup
Quique Flores lines Alaves up in a 4-4-2, with Antonio Sivera in goal and a back four of Hugo Novoa, Facundo Tenaglia, Ville Koski and Jonny Otto. Ángel Hidalgo, Pablo Ibáñez, Antonio Blanco and Abde Rebbach form the midfield bank of four, feeding a forward partnership of Lucas Boyé and Toni Martínez. Facundo Garcés and Mikel Rodríguez are both out, which thins out Flores’ options at the back and in midfield against a Barcelona side set to dominate the ball.
Alaves confirmed starting XI (4-4-2): Antonio Sivera, Hugo Novoa, Facundo Tenaglia, Ville Koski, Jonny Otto, Ángel Hidalgo, Pablo Ibáñez, Antonio Blanco, Abde Rebbach, Lucas Boyé, Toni Martínez. Coach: Quique Flores.

items.title: Why is Manuel Neuer not playing for Bayern Munich vs Borussia Dortmund in 2026-27 Bundesliga?
items.description:
Manuel Neuer is not playing for Bayern Munich against Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga Klassiker, a big absence for a match in which both clubs enter level on points at the top of the table. The veteran captain is out with a persistent foot problem that has kept him away from the team on and […] 
Manuel Neuer is not playing for Bayern Munich against Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga Klassiker, a big absence for a match in which both clubs enter level on points at the top of the table. The veteran captain is out with a persistent foot problem that has kept him away from the team on and off for weeks.



The news was confirmed by assistant coach Aaron Danks, who is standing in for Vincent Kompany, at the pre-match press conference. “It’s coming a bit too early for Manuel Neuer, he still has pain in his foot,” Danks said, adding that the 40-year-old goalkeeper “has to keep watching” how he progresses. The club did not give a timeline for his return.



Neuer has already missed the Champions League match against Viking Stavanger, the Bundesliga games against RB Leipzig and Freiburg, and the cup tie against Magdeburg. He returned to the team for the Champions League game against Arsenal, but has been out again since.



In his absence, Jonas Urbig will start in goal once again against Dortmund. The 22-year-old has stepped in on several occasions this season, and he will now face one of the biggest tests of his young career in a match that could decide who sets the pace at the top of the Bundesliga.




𝐔𝐍𝐒𝐄𝐑𝐄 𝐒𝐓𝐀𝐑𝐓𝐄𝐋𝐅 𝐅𝐔̈𝐑𝐒 𝐓𝐎𝐏𝐒𝐏𝐈𝐄𝐋 𝐆𝐄𝐆𝐄𝐍 𝐃𝐎𝐑𝐓𝐌𝐔𝐍𝐃 🔥👊 pic.twitter.com/fGwN79KGIu— FC Bayern München (@FCBayern) October 31, 2026




Bayern’s injury list ahead of the Klassiker



Neuer is not the only absence for Bayern in the match. Jamal Musiala, Luis Diaz and Bara Ndiaye are also injured, which leaves Danks without several important options for the game.


        


There was good news for the club, however: Joshua Kimmich is in the starting XI after training with the team for the first time on Oct. 30, a quick return that gives Bayern a key piece in midfield for the Klassiker.



Despite the list of absences, Danks was confident ahead of the match. “It’s a big game, the whole world is watching it. We are ready,” he said. Sporting director Max Eberl, for his part, said the equal standing in the table “automatically means a level playing field,” but stressed that the club wants to win and “leave that level playing field”.

items.title: Tottenham vs Crystal Palace: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Premier League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Tottenham vs Crystal Palace in the 2026-27 Premier League. Tottenham host a Crystal Palace side low on confidence, with both managers forced into reshuffles that will shape how this one opens up.
Tottenham come into this match in strong form, having won their last two outings, a 2-0 defeat of Chelsea on October 24 and a 3-1 win over Coventry on October 19, sandwiching a 1-1 draw with Man U before that. The run has lifted the mood around the club heading into this fixture. A win here would make it three in four and keep the pressure on the teams above them.
Crystal Palace arrive in a much tougher spell, having lost their last two games, 0-2 to Newcastle on October 25 and 0-5 to Albion on October 18, a result that came right after a 3-1 win over Nottingham on October 11. The heavy defeat to Albion in particular will have stung Pierre Sage and his squad. Palace need a response here just to steady themselves before the form slide gets any worse.
Tottenham confirmed lineup
De Zerbi sets Tottenham up in a 4-2-3-1, with Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali screening the back four and James Maddison given license to link play behind Omar Marmoush and Dominic Solanke. Mohammed Kudus adds width and direct running from the right, while Pedro Porro and Andy Robertson push on from full back to support the attack. The absence list is long, missing Wilson Odobert, Mykhaylo Mudryk, Savinho, Destiny Udogie, Tosin Adarabioyo, Lucas Bergvall, Xavi Simons, Rodrigo Bentancur and Richarlison, which strips out several attacking and midfield options and leaves the side with little cover if the starters pick up knocks during the game.
Tottenham confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Antonín Kinský, Archie Gray, Jan-Paul van Hecke, Micky van de Ven, Andy Robertson, Mateus Fernandes, Mathys Tel, Sandro Tonali, Mohammed Kudus, Dominic Solanke, Omar Marmoush. Coach: Roberto De Zerbi.
Crystal Palace confirmed lineup
Sage goes with a 3-4-2-1 for Crystal Palace, with Axel Disasi, Chris Richards and Jaydee Canvot forming a back three protected by Adam Wharton in midfield alongside Daichi Kamada. Dwight McNeil and Anan Khalaili provide the width as wing backs, while Yéremy Pino and Tyrick Mitchell work just behind Jean-Philippe Mateta up top. Palace are without Jørgen Strand Larsen, Ismaïla Sarr, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chadi Riad, a group that thins out both their attacking depth and their defensive options from the bench.
Crystal Palace confirmed starting XI (3-4-2-1): Dean Henderson, Óscar Mingueza, Chris Richards, Axel Disasi, Dwight McNeil, Jaydee Canvot, Adam Wharton, Daichi Kamada, Yéremy Pino, Tyrick Mitchell, Jean-Philippe Mateta. Coach: Pierre Sage.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo has had only two years without a hat-trick since 2008: How does Lionel Messi compare?
items.description:
Since Ronaldo recorded his first career hat-trick in 2008, the Portuguese forward has experienced remarkably few calendar years without scoring at least three goals in a single match. 
Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi have spent nearly two decades rewriting soccer’s goalscoring records, but their consistency in front of goal also extends to one particularly impressive statistic. Since Ronaldo recorded his first career hat-trick in 2008, the Portuguese forward has experienced remarkably few calendar years without scoring at least three goals in a single match.



At 41, Ronaldo continues to add to his remarkable collection, with his latest treble for Al-Nassr bringing another milestone within reach. However, Messi has maintained an equally extraordinary record, and the comparison between the two reveals an interesting difference in their consistency.



Ronaldo scored his first official career hat-trick on January 12, 2008, against Newcastle, helping Manchester United secure a 6-0 Premier League victory. He followed that achievement with another prolific period, although 2009 became the first calendar year in which he failed to record a treble. The Portuguese forward then established an incredible run, scoring at least one hat-trick every year from 2010 through 2024.



His most productive period came during his time at Real Madrid, with 2011 standing out as one of his strongest years, when he reportedly scored nine or 10 hat-tricks depending on the statistical source. Ronaldo continued delivering three-goal performances after leaving Madrid, adding to his totals at Juventus, Manchester United, and Al-Nassr.



Ronaldo’s hat-trick to take him to goal 985 🤩 pic.twitter.com/oxgu7aqua2— Roshn Saudi League (@SPL_EN) October 29, 2026



His consistency eventually ended in 2025, when he failed to score a competitive hat-trick despite registering 41 goals across club and international soccer. That made 2025 only the second calendar year without a hat-trick since his first one in 2008. His latest return came on October 29, 2026, when he scored three times in Al-Nassr’s 5-3 Saudi Pro League victory over Al-Kholood.



YearRonaldo’s Hat-tricks200812009020104201110201242013820143201582016720173201832019420201202122022220233202432025020261



Messi has had even fewer blank years



While Ronaldo has gone without a hat-trick in two calendar years since 2008, Messi has had only one blank year since scoring his first career treble in 2007. The Argentine recorded his first hat-trick on March 10, 2007, scoring all three goals in Barcelona’s memorable 3-3 draw against Real Madrid at Camp Nou. He then failed to score another in 2008, before beginning a remarkable sequence that has continued through 2026.



According to messivsronaldo.app, Messi has recorded at least one hat-trick in every calendar year from 2009 to 2026, giving him an 18-year run of annual trebles. His most productive year was 2012, when he scored nine hat-tricks during a period in which he also established the calendar-year record of 91 goals.



YearMessi’s Hat-tricks2007120080200912010420114201292013320143201542016520173201832019420201202112022120231202422025120262



His consistency has survived several major changes throughout his career. The Argentine superstar scored the majority of his hat-tricks at Barcelona, but he continued adding to his tally with La Albiceleste and later Inter Miami, including multiple three-goal performances in MLS.



Two different records, one extraordinary level of consistency



The comparison becomes particularly interesting when looking at the years in which each player failed to score a hat-trick. Ronaldo’s two blank years since 2008 were 2009 and 2025, while Messi’s only blank year after his first treble was 2008. This means the latter’s has maintained a longer uninterrupted sequence of calendar years with at least one hat-trick, stretching from 2009 through 2026.



Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo.



However, Ronaldo still leads in overall career hat-trick numbers according to the supplied figures. His latest performance against Al-Kholood was reported to be his 67th career hat-trick, while Messi’s tally stood at approximately 62.



The figures also highlight how differently their careers have developed. Ronaldo’s most prolific hat-trick years were largely associated with his Real Madrid peak, while Messi’s record has extended across Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain, Inter Miami, and Argentina.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo makes history with 11th perfect hat-trick in career: How many does Lionel Messi have?
items.description:
The Portuguese forward has reached a milestone that highlights his extraordinary versatility in front of goal, adding another record to an already historic collection of scoring achievements. 
Cristiano Ronaldo continues to add remarkable achievements to his career at 41, with another outstanding performance for Al-Nassr reigniting comparisons with longtime rival Lionel Messi. The Portuguese forward has reached a milestone that highlights his extraordinary versatility in front of goal, adding another record to an already historic collection of scoring achievements.



Ronaldo produced the latest display during Al-Nassr’s 5-3 Saudi Pro League victory over Al-Kholood on October 29, 2026. His three second-half goals helped secure the win, but the manner in which he scored them made the occasion particularly memorable.



Al-Nassr’s captain scored all three of his goals within 15 minutes, taking control of the match after Al-Kholood had threatened to make life difficult for the hosts. His first goal arrived in the 66th minute, before he added a header six minutes later and completed the hat-trick with his left foot in the 81st minute.



The combination of finishes made it a perfect hat-trick, a rare achievement that requires a player to score once with each foot and once with their head in the same match. According to multiple statistics outlets, the latest performance brought Ronaldo’s career tally to 11 perfect hat-tricks, the highest figure attributed to any player.



Ronaldo’s hat-trick to take him to goal 985 🤩 pic.twitter.com/oxgu7aqua2— Roshn Saudi League (@SPL_EN) October 29, 2026



The achievement also represented his 67th career hat-trick and his first treble in 908 days, according to the supplied figures. Ronaldo’s three goals took his overall career tally to 985, leaving him just 15 away from the extraordinary milestone of 1,000 official goals.



How many perfect hat-tricks does Lionel Messi have?



While Ronaldo has repeatedly demonstrated his ability to score in different ways, Messi has yet to record a perfect hat-trick during his professional career. The Argentine has zero perfect hat-tricks, despite having scored approximately 62 career hat-tricks.



The contrast is particularly interesting because both players have enjoyed extraordinary longevity and consistently delivered goals at the highest level. Ronaldo’s latest achievement gives him an advantage in this specific category, although it reflects the different characteristics of their playing styles rather than providing a complete measure of their abilities.



Stat CategoryCristiano RonaldoLionel MessiTotal Career Hat-Tricks6762Perfect Hat-Tricks110International Hat-Tricks1011



Messi is predominantly left-footed and has built much of his goalscoring reputation around close control, dribbling, precise finishing and creative movement. Although he has scored with his right foot and produced memorable headers, neither has featured as frequently in his game as his exceptional left-footed finishing.



Lionel Messi of Inter Miami.



Why Ronaldo has the advantage in this category



Ronaldo’s physical attributes and versatility have helped him achieve perfect hat-tricks throughout his career. His aerial ability, powerful jumping, and confidence with both feet make him particularly dangerous in different attacking situations.



Messi, meanwhile, generally operates in positions that allow him to create chances and finish attacks with his preferred foot. He has scored some memorable headers, including his famous goal against Manchester United in the 2009 Champions League final, but aerial finishing has never been a defining part of his game.



That difference helps explain why Ronaldo has reached 11 perfect hat-tricks while Messi remains without one. The statistic highlights Ronaldo’s broader range of finishing methods, rather than establishing superiority in every aspect of goalscoring.

items.title: Neymar reveals what he plans to do after retirement while his future at Santos remains uncertain
items.description:
Neymar revealed in a new interview what he plans to do after retiring and admitted he cannot stand watching soccer on TV, while his future at Santos remains up in the air. 
Neymar has opened up about life after soccer in a new interview, in which he also admitted something few would expect from one of the sport’s biggest stars. The 34-year-old Santos forward spoke with the YouTube program Varanda Gourmet and gave a blunt look at what he wants once his playing days are over.



Although the Brazilian never specified a date for his retirement, Neymar already knows what he will do when he steps away from professional soccer. “When I retire, I’m going to spend a year not doing a damn thing,” he said in the interview.



He insisted that he will not set any routine for that time: “I’m going to do this: if I feel like playing soccer today, I play soccer. If I don’t feel like doing a damn thing today, I do nothing”.



The forward also surprised by saying that he does not enjoy watching soccer on television. “When I said it in interviews or to my friends, nobody believed me. I love soccer, but I love playing it. Sitting on the couch, turning on the TV and watching a match… I can’t,” the Brazilian said.









He recalled his time at Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain, when friends who lived with him watched games on weekends from the morning until the late afternoon. “In Paris and Barcelona, on Saturdays and Sundays there was only soccer on TV. From 11 in the morning until 6 in the afternoon watching soccer… I can’t stand it!” Neymar added.


        


What awaits Neymar at Santos



For now, Neymar remains active, and his contract with Santos runs until Dec. 31, with no confirmation about his next step. The club wants to keep him for 2027, but talks have not advanced, and his continuity is expected to depend largely on the club’s presidential election in December and on a spot in the Copa Libertadores, with interest from the United States also in the background.



A possible retirement is not necessarily tied to the end of his contract, which keeps the door open for him to continue playing or to call it a day. Whatever he decides, Neymar has made one thing clear: when the time comes, he will not rush into his next chapter, and the year he plans to spend away from the game will be on his own terms.

items.title: Lionel Messi could extend his Inter Miami contract beyond 2028 despite reports of a return to Argentina
items.description:
Lionel Messi is very happy at Inter Miami and has no plans to leave, with a contract through 2028 that he could extend, while the club is already planning a future that keeps him tied to the franchise beyond his playing days 
Lionel Messi has no plans to change clubs in the coming months or years, and could even stay at Inter Miami beyond the end of his current contract. According to Fabrizio Romano, the Argentine star is very happy in Florida and is fully focused on the club, despite the reports linking him with a return to Newell’s Old Boys, the first club of his career in Argentina.



Messi’s contract runs until the end of 2028, after he signed a renewal in October 2025, and Romano says the player wants to respect the deal in full. The Italian journalist added that Messi, who is “obviously in control of his future,” could decide later whether to go beyond that date. For now, he said, the intention is to continue at Inter Miami, not to go back to Argentina or join any other club.



The speculation about a return to Rosario began in February, when Newell’s said they had held talks with Messi over an emotional return to the club, with a possible move in the first half of 2027.



Nothing was finalized at the time, and the club’s interest has been one of the biggest storylines around Messi’s future ever since. Romano’s update points in the opposite direction, with the player and his family happy in Miami and no intention of changing anything.




🚨🇦🇷 Leo Messi, not planning Newell’s Old Boys comeback as fully focused on Inter Miami.Messi wants to continue until 2028… and maybe beyond, to be decided later on. pic.twitter.com/nSEsIZRE77— Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) October 30, 2026




A bond that goes beyond football



Messi’s connection with Inter Miami is no longer just about what he does on the pitch. Since arriving in July 2023, the Argentine has become the center of a project that touches the club’s business, its image and its future, and everything suggests that both sides want that relationship to last well beyond his playing days.


        


Romano also noted that Messi is deeply involved in several projects outside the pitch, including the Messi Cup for young talents, which is another reason he is not looking to make changes. At 39, and now that he has retired from the Argentina national team, the captain of Inter Miami is fully focused on the club, which continues to be the face of MLS.



The club shares that vision. According to reports, Inter Miami are already planning a long-term future with Messi that goes beyond his current contract, including the possibility of him joining the ownership group once he stops playing.



Whether it is through a longer contract, a role in the ownership group or the projects he leads away from the pitch, Messi’s future appears tied to Inter Miami for years to come. For now, the only certainty is that he is committed to the club, and that both sides are already building something that will outlast his playing career.

items.title: Football Daily | Newcastle’s Jaissle wants to scream while Grealish leaves Moyes speechless
items.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!While it is customary for fans of top-flight clubs with delusions of grandeur to cope with Fizzy Cup exits by pretending the competition is beneath them, this is no longer an option that is open to supporters of Newcastle United. Winning the trophy sponsored by a low-calorie, fruit-flavoured energy drink brand from Thailand may only rank fifth in the domestic pecking order behind the Premier League, FA Cup and both transfer windows, but nobody will ever forget how much it meant to hundreds of thousands of overjoyed Geordies when their team did exactly that the season before last to end a trophy drought dating back to the Jurassic era. And with a quarter-final trip to the tough-tackling League Two bullyboys of Fleetwood up for grabs during their match against serial trophy-dodgers Everton last night, the travelling Toon Army must have fancied their chances of being in the shake-up again.I clearly remember the first time I laughed out hard and loud, as a 12-year-old, reading Three Men in a Boat by Jerome K Jerome. Tonight, 50 years later, after a stretch of horrendous bad years and months (and for my mental health, I exclude the struggles of Tottenham), I read the Football Daily column. Its is often quite witty, but this time, reading about some penalty kick gone awry … I know, I have a simplistic sense of humour, but I laughed so hard and cried at the same time, that my family wondered what happened. Thanks for a cathartic experience. Words” – L Json.As a Spurs supporter who saw my first game at White Hart Lane when I was five years old – almost eight decades ago – I can only express my relief that attention has drifted away from the continual ridicule of my team. The fact that a certain club that should return to south of the Thames managed to lose at Highbury (ironically), that lot from down Kings Road and Manchester United are all hogging the headlines for all the wrong reasons just makes life sweeter. It’s time for my second nap of the day now, so I’ll sign off” – Stewart McGuinness.This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. items.title: Lionel Messi avoids suspension for crucial Inter Miami vs New England clash despite fifth yellow card
items.description:
Lionel Messi received his fifth yellow card in Inter Miami’s 2-2 draw with Cincinnati but will not miss the crucial match against New England thanks to an MLS rule that rewards good behavior. 
Lionel Messi will be available for Inter Miami’s decisive match against New England Revolution on Nov. 1, even though he received his fifth yellow card of the MLS season in the 2-2 draw with FC Cincinnati.



The Argentine captain avoids a suspension thanks to a league rule that rewards good behavior, a relief for the Herons as they fight for a place in next year’s Concacaf Champions Cup.



Messi was booked in the 44th minute at Nu Stadium, adding to the yellow cards he had already received in matchweeks 8, 11, 20 and 31, and the one he got in matchweek 33.



Under MLS rules, a player automatically reduces his yellow card total by one each time he appears in five consecutive matches without receiving a yellow card, a red card or supplemental discipline. The incentive can be applied a maximum of three times in the regular season.



How did Messi gets a yellow card for this man???????? pic.twitter.com/G2upkM56gQ— LSPN_FC (@LSPN__FC_12) October 29, 2026 



Messi went more than five games without a booking on two occasions, so two of his five cards no longer count toward the accumulation that would force him to miss a match. 


        


The bookings remain on his disciplinary record, but they no longer put him at risk of a suspension, which keeps him available for a game in which Inter Miami cannot afford to be without their best player.



What is at stake for Inter Miami in New England



For Messi and Inter Miami, the importance of the match goes far beyond three points. The trip to Gillette Stadium could decide whether the Herons play on the continental stage next year, and the Argentine captain’s availability could not come at a better time.



Inter Miami sit third in the Eastern Conference, two points behind New England, and both teams have already qualified for the MLS playoffs. The Champions Cup is another story. Nashville have secured the Supporters’ Shield, which means second place in the East will earn one of the automatic spots, making the match in New England crucial for both sides.



Head coach Cristian “Kily” Gonzalez said after the draw with Cincinnati that his team no longer has any margin for error in the final two games of the regular season. 



“I am convinced that the frustration we feel, just like after the previous match, must make us stronger, because we no longer have any margin for error. We need to realize that we are a club that has to step forward, take risks, show personality and play football without fear of making mistakes,” explained the Argentine coach.



With Messi cleared to play, Inter Miami head to New England knowing that a win could change the outlook of their season, while a slip could leave them chasing a Champions Cup spot in the final matchday. The Herons still control their own destiny, but after a late draw with Cincinnati, there is little room for anything other than three points.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo scores hat-trick in 15 minutes for Al Nassr: How does it compare with Lionel Messi’s fastest?
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo scored a hat-trick in 15 minutes for Al Nassr and not even this was the quickest treble of his own career. 
Cristiano Ronaldo scored a hat-trick in just 15 minutes for Al Nassr in their 5-3 win over Al Kholood, a burst that took him to 985 career goals. It was a remarkable display of efficiency from the 41-year-old, but how does it compare with the fastest treble of his great rival, Lionel Messi?



With the match tied 2-2, Ronaldo scored in the 66th, 72nd and 81st minutes to take control of the Saudi Pro League clash at Alawwal Park. The first two goals were set up by Joao Felix, who finished the night with four assists, and the third came from a Sadio Mane pass.



Messi’s fastest hat-trick came more recently, in October 2024 for Inter Miami, when he needed only 11 minutes to score three goals in a 6-2 win over New England Revolution after coming on in the 57th minute.



The Argentine also has a treble that took a very similar amount of time for Barcelona, when he needed 13 minutes in a 2014-15 league match against Rayo Vallecano at Camp Nou.



Ronaldo's hat trick on Thursday leaves him only 15 away from reaching 1,000 career goals. pic.twitter.com/aF44xW3Asu— FOX Soccer (@FOXSoccer) October 29, 2026 



Not even Ronaldo’s fastest hat-trick



Despite scoring three goals in just 15 minutes, this was not the fastest hat-trick of Ronaldo’s own career either. His best mark came in 2015, when he scored his first three goals in eight minutes for Real Madrid against Granada, in a match he finished with five goals, the highest tally of his career in a single game, a mark he also reached against Espanyol.


        


With his latest treble against Al Kholood, Ronaldo reached 67 career hat-tricks. He now has 44 for Real Madrid, 10 for Portugal, seven for Al Nassr, three for Manchester United and three for Juventus, according to ESPN.



With both legends in the final stretch of their careers, every performance like this one adds a new chapter to the debate over who is the greatest of all time. Ronaldo is now 15 goals away from 1,000, while Messi sits on 936, and neither seems ready to slow down. The fast hat-tricks may not be as frequent as they once were, but as long as both keep scoring, the comparisons will continue.

items.title: Joao Felix makes Saudi Pro League history as Cristiano Ronaldo leads Al Nassr to a 5-3 win vs Al Kholood
items.description:
Joao Felix became the third player to record four assists in a single Saudi Pro League match, two of them for Cristiano Ronaldo’s hat-trick, as Al Nassr beat Al Kholood 5-3. 
Joao Felix made Saudi Pro League history, becoming the third player to record four assists in a single league match as Al Nassr beat Al Kholood 5-3 in Round 12 at Alawwal Park. The Portuguese playmaker was involved in four of the five goals, while his compatriot Cristiano Ronaldo scored a hat-trick to lead the hosts to the win.



According to The Nassr Tribune, only two players had previously reached that mark in the competition: Youssef El Gharbi in 2011 and Moussa Diaby in 2024. Felix’s first assist came in the 24th minute, when he sent a heel pass to Angelo, who equalized after Al Kholood had taken the lead. In the 38th minute, his first-time attempt from a cross turned into an involuntary assist for Sadio Mane, who put Al Nassr ahead.



The other two assists went to Ronaldo, who scored in the 66th and 72nd minutes to turn a 2-2 match into a 4-2 lead. The forward completed his hat-trick in the 81st minute, this time with an assist from Mane, and Al Kholood pulled one back late.



The win sends Al Nassr to the top of the Saudi Pro League table, at least until Al Hilal face Al Fateh, and it was a night for Felix to remember. The former Chelsea and Barcelona forward has been one of the league’s most productive playmakers since joining Al Nassr, and his performance against Al Kholood now stands alongside the best individual displays the league has seen.




João Félix writes his name into Saudi League history.. four assists in one night 🪄 pic.twitter.com/fcnTez8Kle— AlNassr FC (@AlNassrFC_EN) October 29, 2026




Joao Felix keeps shining after a Player of the Season campaign



Last season, Felix was named the Saudi Pro League Player of the Season in his debut year at Al Nassr, an award he received a day after the club clinched the league title. He finished the campaign with 26 goals and 19 assists in 47 matches across all competitions, according to Transfermarkt, including 20 goals in the league.


        


His form has carried over to the new campaign. So far this season, the Portuguese playmaker has 5 goals and 8 assists in 13 matches in all competitions, including 3 goals and 7 assists in 10 Saudi Pro League appearances, in what is shaping up to be another standout year for Al Nassr’s number 79.



With the performance against Al Kholood, Felix added another highlight to a partnership with Ronaldo that continues to pay off for Al Nassr. The two Portuguese stars have become a constant threat for opposing defenses, and the record-tying night showed how well they connect when the team is at its best. As the title race heats up, Al Nassr will hope to keep that chemistry going, with Felix creating chances and Ronaldo finishing them.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo climbs the Saudi Pro League Golden Boot race with hat-trick for Al Nassr vs Al Kholood
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo scored a hat-trick in Al Nassr’s 5-3 win over Al Kholood, moving up the Golden Boot race and reaching 985 career goals, though the Saudi Pro League’s official records do not yet credit him with all of them. 
Cristiano Ronaldo took a big step in the Saudi Pro League Golden Boot race with a hat-trick in Al Nassr’s 5-3 win over Al Kholood, a performance that also took him to 985 career goals. The Portuguese forward scored three times in 15 minutes after the hour mark in Round 12 at Alawwal Park, in his first match since winning the Ballon d’Or of All Time award.



Ronaldo put Al Nassr 3-2 ahead in the 66th minute with an assist from Joao Felix, added a second in the 72nd, again set up by Felix, and completed the hat-trick in the 81st minute with an assist from Sadio Mane.



The hat-trick lifts him to 7 league goals in the official standings, level with Mateo Retegui and Youssef En-Nesyri and one behind Tijjani Reijnders, who has 8. Ivan Toney remains well ahead with 12, although Ronaldo has played one more match than the Englishman, who has 9 appearances to the forward’s 10.



If the goal from the previous match against Al Faisaly is counted, Ronaldo would have 8 and would be level with Reijnders in second place, while Toney would have 13, so the gap to the top would stay at five goals.



Saudi Pro League’s top scorers according to the official website.



The goals the Saudi Pro League took away



Not every record agrees on the tally. In the 3-1 win over Al Faisaly on Oct. 23, Ronaldo headed home from a Felix free kick, but replays suggested the ball may have come off defender Andrei Girotto, and the league ultimately recorded it as an own goal.


        


Toney’s case is almost identical: his header in Al Ahli’s 4-1 win over Al Khaleej was reviewed by VAR before it was confirmed, but it was later reclassified as an own goal too. The Saudi Pro League’s official website and statistics pages such as Transfermarkt currently do not credit those goals to either striker, as the table shows. 



Journalists such as Fabrizio Romano, however, do credit them and report that Ronaldo reached 985 career goals with tonight’s hat-trick. Until the official records are updated, the debate over the totals will continue, both for the Golden Boot race and for Ronaldo’s march toward 1,000.

items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo scored a hat-trick for Al Nassr in their Round 12 clash against Al Kholood, reaching his 985th career goal. 
Cristiano Ronaldo scored a hat-trick for Al Nassr in their 5-3 win over Al Kholood in Round 12 of the Saudi Pro League at Alawwal Park in Riyadh, reaching his 985th career goal. The Portuguese forward found the net three times in 15 minutes after the hour mark, in his first match since winning the Ballon d’Or of All Time award.



The first half was chaotic. Ronaldo had a goal ruled out for offside early on, and Julien Domingues put Al Kholood ahead soon after. Angelo then equalized from a Joao Felix assist, Sadio Mane turned the match around on the counter-attack, and Loic Essomba tied it at 2-2 just before the break. 



Ronaldo had another goal disallowed for offside right after the equalizer, meaning he had two chalked off in the first half and three in his last two matches.



He made up for it after the break. Ronaldo put Al Nassr 3-2 ahead in the 66th minute with an assist from Felix, added a second in the 72nd to make it 4-2, again set up by Felix, and completed the hat-trick in the 81st minute with an assist from Mane. Al Kholood pulled one back late, but Al Nassr held on for a 5-3 win that sends them to the top of the Saudi Pro League table, at least until Al Hilal face Al Fateh.

Why the Saudi Pro League’s count differs



The 985 figure counts a goal in the 3-1 win over Al Faisaly on Oct. 23 that the Saudi Pro League did not record as Ronaldo’s. Although some journalists in Saudi Arabia claim the league credited the goal to the Portuguese star, the league’s official website listed him with four goals this season instead of five before tonight’s match. By the official count, the hat-trick takes him to 984 career goals, one fewer than the total reported by Fabrizio Romano and other outlets.


        


At 41, he continues to score at a steady pace for Al Nassr, who have won four in a row and are chasing the league leaders in the title race. Whether the Saudi Pro League eventually changes its records or not, the Portuguese star appears to be moving closer to the historic mark with every match.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo scores 67th career hat-trick: How his record compares to Lionel Messi
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo netted the 67th hat-trick of his legendary career to fire Al Nassr to a 5-3 victory over Al Kholood, widening his advantage over longtime rival Lionel Messi. 
Cristiano Ronaldo remains soccer’s ultimate scoring machine. In Al Nassr’s pulsating 5–3 victory over Al Kholood, the Portuguese icon produced his 67th career hat-trick, extending his cushion over Lionel Messi at the summit of the sport’s all-time treble leaderboard.



On his relentless march toward 1,000 official career goals, Ronaldo delivered a vintage second-half clinic at Alawwal Park, bagging three goals in a devastating 15-minute blitz to secure three crucial points for Al Nassr in the 2026–27 Saudi Pro League.



Reaching 67 career hat-tricks creates further daylight between Ronaldo and Lionel Messi, who sits on 62 career trebles across his legendary stints with Barcelona, Inter Miami, and Argentina. While the two icons have traded statistical records for nearly two decades, Ronaldo’s latest milestone reaffirms his unmatched volume as a pure penalty-box marksman



The race to 1,000 career goals heats up



While Ronaldo enters every campaign chasing team silverware, his most historic personal pursuit remains the unprecedented quest to breach the 1,000-goal barrier—a benchmark never verified in top-tier professional football.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr.



Following Thursday’s treble, Ronaldo stands at 985 official career goals for club and country. With more than half of the domestic season remaining, continental fixtures on the horizon, and an active role with the Portugal national team, the 41-year-old is firmly on course to eclipse the four-figure mark before the 2026–27 campaign concludes.


        


Ronaldo recently hinted that this season may well be his last as a professional player, adding dramatic urgency to every appearance. If he crowns his extraordinary career by becoming the first player in history to score 1,000 official goals, he will have conquered football’s final statistical frontier, paving the way for a fitting farewell at the pinnacle of the sport.

items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Al Nassr vs Al Kholood in the 2026-27 Saudi Pro League. Al Nassr host Al Kholood with the gap between the two clubs already wide on form, and this projected lineup suggests Ange Postecoglou sees no reason to change a winning approach.
Al Nassr come into this one on a three-match winning run. They beat Al-Faisaly 3-1 on October 23, followed a 1-0 win over Neom SC on October 20, and opened that stretch with a 3-0 win over Al Diriyah on October 9. A fourth straight win would keep them firmly in the title picture.
Al Kholood arrive in far worse shape, having lost three in a row. They fell 0-3 to Al-Ettifaq on October 24, were beaten 2-3 by Al-Faisaly on October 15, and before that suffered a heavy 0-5 defeat to Al Qadsiah on October 9. Des Buckingham needs a response just to stop the slide.
Al Nassr confirmed lineup
Postecoglou lines Al Nassr up in a 4-4-2 built around Cristiano Ronaldo and Sadio Mane up front, with Joao Felix and Abdullah Al-Khaibari asked to supply width and link play from midfield. Inigo Martinez anchors the back line alongside Abdulelah Al Amri, giving the side experience at the center of defense. There are no absences listed, so Postecoglou has his strongest group available to press home the advantage in form.
Al Nassr confirmed starting XI (4-4-2): Milan Borjan, Awad Dahal, Hussain Qassem, Kader Keita, Hussam Majrashi, Rodrigo Abascal, Fahad Al Jayzani, Victor Lekhal, Trezeguet, Teddy Okou, Bernard Mensah. Coach: Maurício Corrêa Dulac.
Al Kholood confirmed lineup
Buckingham sets Al Kholood up in a 4-3-3, with Coba da Costa leading the line and Julien Domingues and Gustavo Rodrigues providing support from wide areas. John Buckley and Iker Kortajarena sit in midfield to try to control possession against a stronger opponent. With no absences reported, Buckingham can pick from a full squad as he looks to end a three-game losing run.
Al Kholood confirmed starting XI (3-5-2): Koen Casteels, Mohammed Abu Al Shamat, Christopher Bonsu Baah, Gastón Álvarez, Jehad Thakri, Yasser Al Shahrani, Musab Al Juwayr, Tijjani Reijnders, Julián Quiñones, Abdullah Al Salem, Julian Weigl. Coach: Brendan Rodgers.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo reacts to winning the BOAT award after beating Lionel Messi in the vote
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo has reacted to being named the winner of the Ballon d’Or of All Time award, dedicating the recognition to the supporters. The Portuguese star shared his message on his X account, a day after the result of the public vote was announced. “Football belongs to the fans! Thank you to all the fans […] 
Cristiano Ronaldo has reacted to being named the winner of the Ballon d’Or of All Time award, dedicating the recognition to the supporters. The Portuguese star shared his message on his X account, a day after the result of the public vote was announced.



“Football belongs to the fans! Thank you to all the fans around the world, the Ballon D’Or of All Time is also yours,” Ronaldo wrote. The post, which quickly passed 1.6 million views, was his first public comment since the award was confirmed.



The B.O.A.T. (Best of All Time) prize was decided in an online vote on the official Ballon d’Or website, where fans chose the best individual season among 10 players who had won the Ballon d’Or at least twice.



Ronaldo’s 2008 campaign with Manchester United, which earned him his first Ballon d’Or, finished first, leaving Lionel Messi’s 2012 season in second place, while Ronaldo’s 2017 edition placed third.




Football belongs to the fans! Thank you to all the fans around the world, the Ballon D’Or of All Time is also yours. pic.twitter.com/S0sLDNiUUY— Cristiano Ronaldo (@Cristiano) October 29, 2026




A fan vote, not an official Ballon d’Or



It is worth noting that, unlike the traditional Ballon d’Or categories, which are decided by a panel of journalists, the B.O.A.T. does not count as an official award in the same way. It reflects the preference of the fans who took part rather than a formal ruling, which is why it does not change the official tally of Ronaldo’s individual honors.


        


That tally stands at five Ballon d’Ors: the 2008 award with United and four more in 2013, 2014, 2016 and 2017 during his time at Real Madrid. The English club also celebrated the result on its official website, and the Portuguese national team had congratulated its captain in a message of its own.



With the award now added to his résumé, Ronaldo turns his attention back to the pitch, where he is chasing another milestone. The 41-year-old forward sits on 981 career goals, 19 short of 1,000, and continues to lead Al Nassr’s push to defend the Saudi Pro League title, while his future with Portugal remains uncertain after his suspension.

items.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
items.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadowsShould any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile.Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure. Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door. Continue reading...

items.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
items.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written.“The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

items.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
items.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast teamSign up for our free newsletter hereFor two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes.This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

items.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
items.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community  still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career“The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.”McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well).The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players.The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
